issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the narrative text elsewhere says animals only share a name. The provided solution implements Animal with only a name and a constructor Animal(String). This mismatch (attributes and constructor parameters) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about whether Animal must include an age field and a two-argument constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and template consistent. Either (A) update the problem UML and any textual references to remove the 'age' attribute and require a single-argument constructor Animal(String), or (B) update the solution and template to include the 'age' attribute and a constructor Animal(String, int), plus corresponding getter/setter. Ensure all places (UML, textual description, template stubs, and solution) agree on the attributes and constructor signature.

issues.description: The template Farm.java declares a helper method singFarmSongVerse with the parameter commented out (no formal parameter), while the problem UML and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch in the method signature between template and specification/solution could prevent students from following the intended implementation and cause confusion about how to implement verse printing.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the UML and solution: declare the method as private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (uncomment the parameter). This aligns the template with the specification and lets students implement verse printing using the provided Animal parameter.

issues.description: The problem UML specifies Animal has two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the solution implements Animal with only a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and no age attribute. The template Main also uses single-argument constructors for derived animals. This mismatch between the problem specification and the provided/solution code creates confusion about the required Animal API (constructor signature and attributes) and which implementation students should follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and code: either update the problem UML to require only a name (Animal(String)) and remove the age attribute, or update the template and solution to include the age attribute and constructor Animal(String, int) (and update all derived class constructors and example usages in Main accordingly).
